back: The increasing worldwide integration of economies through trade, investment, movement of people and the spread of technology.
Improved transport links; technological change including communication; free trade agreements; newly industrialised countries.
An agreement between countries to reduce or remove trade barriers, such as tariffs and quotas, between them.
A country whose economy has quickly moved from agriculture and raw materials towards manufacturing and world trade.

front: Opportunities of globalisation for a business?
back: New markets, cheaper inputs, economies of scale, production abroad, new technology, partnerships.

front: Threats of globalisation for a business?
back: More competition from imports and multinationals, competition for workers, takeovers, exchange-rate risk, dependence on distant suppliers.

front: How can a local firm respond to cheaper imports?
back: Improve quality and efficiency, focus on a niche, market its local advantage, export, form partnerships.
The internet, mobile communication and e-payments let firms find, serve and be paid by customers anywhere.
